document.abstract: In February of 1975, CBS issued target specifications for the design of a videotape recorder with improved editing capabilities. The thrust of these specifications was for a recorder with vastly improved transport characteristics, coupled with a tape format which would permit the display of viewable pictures at a variety of speeds in both forward and reverse. The intended application was for off-line editing systems from which a work copy would be produced. The camera originals would later be conformed through automatic assembly in an on-line editing system.

authors.affiliation: CBS Television Network New York, N.Y.
authors.bio: William G. Connolly received his degree in Mathematics from Columbia University, New York City, in January 1957, after a four-year tour of duty with the United States Air Force. He joined the CBS Television Network in 1960 after four years with the Automation Applications Department of the Western Union Telegraph Company. In 1965, he became Associate Director of Engineering for the CBS Television Stations Division and subsequently returned to the television network to assume his present post of Director of Development, in the Engineering and Development Division. In this post, he is responsible for the development of all new components and systems for use in the technical facilities throughout the network. Mr. Connolly was the recipient of an Emmy Award for the development of the CBS Color Corrector in 1971. He resides in Garden City, New York with his wife Lorraine and his six children – Virginia, Michael, Kathleen, Patricia, Peter and Susan.
